name: split_string_class
expr: p1 = split("a,b,c",","); c1 = double(isstring(p1)); n1 = numel(p1); f1 = double(char(p1(3))); p2 = split('a,b,c',','); c2 = double(iscell(p2)); f2 = double(p2{2}); p3 = split("a b c"); n3 = numel(p3); c3 = double(isstring(p3));
comment: split output-class preservation vs MATLAB R2025b. DEEP-PROBE 2026-05-31: numkit's split always returned a CELL, but MATLAB returns a STRING array when the input is a string and a cell array of char vectors only for char/cellstr input (doc: 'If str is a string array, then newStr is a string array. Otherwise, newStr is a cell array of character vectors.'). Values + N x 1 shape were already correct; only the container class was wrong. split("a,b,c",",") -> 3x1 string ["a";"b";"c"] (isstring=1); split('a,b,c',',') -> 3x1 cell (iscell=1); split("a b c") (default whitespace) -> 3x1 string. f1=double('c')=99, f2=double('b')=98. The 2-D string-ARRAY input form (split(["a-b";"c-d"],"-") -> 2x2) is a separate, larger feature deferred to a future cycle. covers:[split].
